name: Helen Keller Intl vitamin A supplementation (The Life You Can Save, 2025)
beneficiaries_note: The 13 countries in the sheet's summary, weighted by Helen Keller Intl's cost in each.

missing_data.note: Measured: Helen Keller Intl counts the children given capsules in each country, and the mortality effect is from trials of the same supplementation.

summary: Helen Keller Intl supports governments' twice-yearly campaigns that give children aged 6 to 59 months vitamin A capsules. The Life You Can Save estimates a cost per DALY averted in each of 13 African countries from Helen Keller Intl's 2024 costs and children reached, a 12% fall in child deaths for the six months a dose protects, and each country's child death rate. Our view values the deaths averted the site's way and takes out the doses governments would have given anyway; the biggest uncertainties are how much vitamin A still cuts deaths where deficiency has fallen and how much of the coverage is Helen Keller Intl's doing.

sections.title: Effect of a dose
sections.explainer: The Life You Can Save's estimate: vitamin A capsules cut child deaths by 12% for the six months a dose lasts, applied to each country's child death rate.

sections.title: The Life You Can Save's bottom line
Deaths valued the site's way
sections.explainer: charityevals' step: each death averted is valued like every child's death on the site, the doses that would have been given anyway taken out, and a small side effect for vitamin A's other benefits.

sections.title: Costs the sheet leaves out
sections.explainer: charityevals' step: Helen Keller Intl's central costs, and with credit by share of resources on, its staff's pay below market and the governments' and donors' share.

Cost per DALY averted, the 13 countries pooled by their money
rows.formula: (cost_burkina_faso + cost_cameroon + cost_cote_divoire + cost_drc + cost_guinea + cost_kenya + cost_madagascar + cost_mali + cost_niger + cost_nigeria + cost_mozambique + cost_sierra_leone + cost_tanzania) / (dalys_burkina_faso + dalys_cameroon + dalys_cote_divoire + dalys_drc + dalys_guinea + dalys_kenya + dalys_madagascar + dalys_mali + dalys_niger + dalys_nigeria + dalys_mozambique + dalys_sierra_leone + dalys_tanzania)
rows.explainer: The sheet gives a cost per DALY for each country (from $12 in Niger to $138 in Mozambique) and no overall figure. This row is our pooling of its figures: all 13 countries' costs over all their DALYs, what the average dollar did. Senegal is left out as in the sheet's summary: its reach wasn't reported (a health workers' strike).

rows.label: Value of averting a child's death, in healthy years
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The Life You Can Save counts a child's death averted as its remaining life expectancy at age 2.5, discounted at 3% (27.9 to 28.9 years). The site values every child's death the same way: GiveWell's moral weight for a death under five times the value-of-a-life slider, in healthy years.

rows.label: Good of vitamin A beyond deaths averted, as a share of it
rows.explainer: The sheet counts only deaths. Vitamin A also prevents night blindness and xerophthalmia and shortens measles and diarrhoea; our judgment puts these at 5% (0 to 15%) of the deaths' value.

rows.label: Share of the children reached who wouldn't have had vitamin A without Helen Keller Intl
rows.explainer: The sheet credits Helen Keller Intl with every child reached. Governments run the campaigns, UNICEF and Nutrition International supply the capsules, and coverage was already 80–100% in most of these countries before the year counted (the sheet's own baseline row); our judgment is that 70% (40 to 100%) of the doses wouldn't have been given without Helen Keller Intl's support.

rows.label: Our healthy years for the same deaths, as a share of The Life You Can Save's DALYs
rows.explainer: The evaluator view keeps The Life You Can Save's (1).

rows.label: Helen Keller Intl's spending beyond the country costs, per dollar of them
rows.explainer: The country costs may leave out Helen Keller Intl's headquarters, management and fundraising, about a tenth of its spending; our judgment, 10% (0 to 20%).

rows.label: Others' cost per child reached (governments' health workers, donated capsules)
rows.explainer: Governments' staff run the campaigns and the capsules are donated; with credit by share of resources on, their money shares the outcome. Our judgment of their cost per child reached in a round.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for programs where staff deliver the help themselves; Helen Keller Intl's staff train, supervise and monitor the campaigns. Our judgment.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Health workers and field staff at nonprofits. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Children reached, the 13 countries
rows.formula: reached_burkina_faso + reached_cameroon + reached_cote_divoire + reached_drc + reached_guinea + reached_kenya + reached_madagascar + reached_mali + reached_niger + reached_nigeria + reached_mozambique + reached_sierra_leone + reached_tanzania

rows.label: Full cost per dollar of the sheet's costs
rows.formula: (cost_total * (1 + central_cost_share) * (1 + if($resource_shares, salary_sacrifice, 0)) + if($resource_shares, others_cost_per_child * reached_total, 0)) / cost_total
rows.explainer: Central costs always; with credit by share of resources on, staff's forgone pay and others' money as well.

rows.label: DALYs averted per dollar
rows.explainer: The Life You Can Save's pooled DALYs per dollar, deaths valued the site's way, after what would have happened anyway and all costs.
